title: Small developement tip (create your own skills)
author: yanenrogne
selftext:
Hey! Here's a little tip that helped me while developing a game. Some of you might already know this, but hopefully it helps someone!

If you notice you keep doing something repeatedly, consider asking the AI to create a skill that does it for you, with rules specific to your project.

For example, I kept taking screenshots of my game's UI to show the AI what I was talking about. So I asked it to create a skill where it launches the game itself, navigates to the relevant screen, takes a screenshot, and analyzes it. That sped up development and debugging by a solid amount.

You can also create skills for generating images/sprites/icons — for instance, a skill that already knows your art style, color palette, and resolution requirements so you don't have to re-explain your whole project every time.

If you already do this and have cool skill ideas, I'd love to hear them!

comments.author: alta_01
comments.body:
There's a Godot MCP project that can drive a lot of the debugging. Saves me a ton of time and includes screenshots.

To your point though, I always try and make a skill file.or update an existing one after completing a task to log all the gotchas. Make sure that the skill file being created is a pointer file to reference docs so that you don't load a massive skill file every single and clog context until you compact

comments.author: Kingnorik
comments.body: First thing I do is ask it for a "tunnel" for testing.

replies.author: yanenrogne
replies.body: What do you mean by that?

replies.author: Kingnorik
replies.body: For instance Godot. I'm making an RTS, it makes a scene called arena that it can freely load all the units to test their combat functionality. Super lightweight and easy to debug.

replies.author: yanenrogne
replies.body: Ah yes I understand, good idea! I'm making an incremental game and made various game states I can load to test balancing numbers =)

replies.author: yanenrogne
replies.body:

Posted about it here https://www.reddit.com/r/IndieDev/s/UzfI6nFjxu

comments.author: Uncled1023
comments.body: Along with this, if it's something that can be scripted, have the ai make a script for it.  Makes it actually reproducible, and scripts don't use tokens.

comments.author: NullzeroJP
comments.body:
After every feature is implemented, I ask the model what gotchas and traps did it run into, and what part of the implementation took the most turns to get right. The propose a list of those gotchas to add to the agents.md.

Then if there are any items that sound general enough that future agents will run into them, I ask the agent to add that item to the agents.md

Just be careful, because you also have to prune the list once a week or so… when my agents.md starts ballooning to 35kb or higher, I start considering a prune session.
